title: Small Business Runway Extension Act of 2018
official_summary:
Small Business Runway Extension Act of 2018

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the Small Business Act to revise certain requirements for prescribing size standards for small businesses. Such standards shall be calculated using average annual gross receipts of such businesses from at least the previous five (currently, three) years.

summary.headline: This law changes how the Small Business Administration measures whether a business counts as small, using a longer five-year average of its receipts.
summary.what_it_does: The law amends the Small Business Act, which governs how the federal government defines a small business. It changes the rules for setting size standards so they use average annual gross receipts over at least the previous five years. The current rule uses three years. The official summary does not describe any other changes.

who_it_affects.group: Small businesses that seek to qualify as small under federal size standards
who_it_affects.how: Their eligibility may be judged using a five-year average of gross receipts instead of a three-year average.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses that bid on or hold federal contracts set aside for small businesses
who_it_affects.how: Whether they meet small business size limits for those contracts may depend on the longer averaging period.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies and the Small Business Administration
who_it_affects.how: They must calculate size standards using the five-year receipts period when they set or revise those standards.
